papers.paper: Tri Dao, "FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning", 2023, arXiv:2307.08691
papers.verify_evidence: arxiv.org/abs/2307.08691 -> title 'FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning', author Tri Dao. Source docstring cites the flash2 whitepaper URL, whose canonical arXiv id is 2307.08691.
papers.source_excerpt: 06-fused-attention.py:5  "This is a Triton implementation of the Flash Attention v2 algorithm from Tri Dao (https://tridao.me/publications/flash2/flash2.pdf)"
papers.grounding_rationale: The kernel IS FlashAttention-2: the tl_attn_fwd/_attn_bwd inner loop performs the block-wise softmax with running max/sum rescaling. A reader cannot follow the acc-rescale / l_i / m_i bookkeeping without a dedicated原理章 deriving the online-softmax tiling and the v2 work-partitioning (parallelize over seq, keep softmax stats in registers).

papers.paper: Tri Dao, Daniel Y. Fu, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, Christopher Ré, "FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness", NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2205.14135
papers.verify_evidence: arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135 -> title 'FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness', authors Dao, Fu, Ermon, Rudra, Ré.
papers.grounding_rationale: v1 introduces the IO-aware tiling + recomputation-in-backward that the v2 kernel inherits; belongs in the same FlashAttention primer chapter as the foundational derivation (block softmax, no full N×N materialization).

papers.paper: Markus N. Rabe, Charles Staats, "Self-attention Does Not Need O(n^2) Memory", 2021, arXiv:2112.05682
papers.verify_evidence: arxiv.org/abs/2112.05682 -> title 'Self-attention Does Not Need $O(n^2)$ Memory', authors Markus N. Rabe and Charles Staats.
papers.grounding_rationale: Predecessor 'lazy softmax' rescaling idea; a 3-5 sentence box (running numerator/denominator + max-shift, constant memory) inside the FlashAttention primer suffices — it is context, not a separate chapter.

tutorial_spine_bindings.teaching_topic: LayerNorm forward + fused backward (weight/bias grads, welford-free two-pass)

papers.paper: Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros, Geoffrey E. Hinton, "Layer Normalization", 2016, arXiv:1607.06450
papers.verify_evidence: arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450 -> title 'Layer Normalization', authors Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros, Geoffrey E. Hinton. Source writes '[BA2016] ... "Layer Normalization", Arxiv 2016'.
papers.source_excerpt: 05-layer-norm.py:374  ".. [BA2016] Jimmy Lei Ba and Jamie Ryan Kiros and Geoffrey E. Hinton, \"Layer Normalization\", Arxiv 2016"
papers.grounding_rationale: The forward formula (normalize over feature dim, affine γ/β) is standard; a prereq-box giving y=(x-μ)/√(σ²+ε)·w+b plus the dx/dw/db gradient identities is enough. The tutorial's interesting part (the fused backward reduction / partial-grad accumulation across program instances) is engineering the book can teach in-chapter, not paper-theory.

tutorial_spine_bindings.teaching_topic: Seeded, stateless (counter-based RNG) low-memory dropout — regenerate mask from an int32 seed instead of storing it

papers.paper: John K. Salmon, Mark A. Moraes, Ron O. Dror, David E. Shaw, "Parallel Random Numbers: As Easy as 1, 2, 3", SC 2011, DOI 10.1145/2063384.2063405 (introduces Philox — the CBRNG behind Triton tl.rand)
papers.verify_evidence: WebSearch confirms ACM DL 10.1145/2063384.2063405, SC'11 Best Paper, authors Salmon/Moraes/Dror/Shaw, introduces Philox counter-based RNG (Random123). Matches source [SALMON2011] verbatim.
papers.source_excerpt: 04-low-memory-dropout.py:172  ".. [SALMON2011] John K. Salmon, Mark A. Moraes, Ron O. Dror, and David E. Shaw, \"Parallel Random Numbers: As Easy as 1, 2, 3\", 2011"
papers.where_used: python/tutorials/04-low-memory-dropout.py:169-172 (References). Load-bearing: the whole tutorial premise (stateless mask from a seed) relies on Triton's tl.rand, a Philox counter-based generator from this paper.
papers.grounding_rationale: A prereq-box explaining counter-based / stateless RNG (output = f(key=seed, counter=offset), no carried state → reproducible mask without storing it) is the conceptual key that makes the tutorial click. Not a full chapter.

papers.paper: Nitish Srivastava, Geoffrey Hinton, Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, "Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting", JMLR 2014
papers.verify_evidence: Written verbatim in source References [SRIVASTAVA2014] with venue JMLR 2014; not independently re-fetched (no arXiv id given). Well-known JMLR v15 paper.
papers.source_excerpt: 04-low-memory-dropout.py:173  ".. [SRIVASTAVA2014] Nitish Srivastava and Geoffrey Hinton and Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever and Ruslan Salakhutdinov, \"Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting\", JMLR 2014"
papers.grounding_rationale: Dropout itself is background; the tutorial is about the RNG memory trick, not dropout regularization theory. One-line citation ('dropout, per Srivastava et al. 2014') suffices; the 1/(1-p) scaling is explained in-text at line 30.

tutorial_spine_bindings.teaching_topic: vector add / fused softmax / tiled matmul (L2 swizzle) / libdevice extern / grouped GEMM (static device-side scheduling) / persistent + TMA + warp-specialized matmul
tutorial_spine_bindings.no_paper_note: These tutorials cite NO academic papers in their docstrings — they are pure engineering walk-throughs (grep for arxiv/doi/reference/et-al returns only URLs to CUDA/HIP/PyTorch docs, not papers). Grounding for these chapters is 'none' (self-contained source reading). Two implicit-but-uncited algorithm lineages worth an editorial call, NOT source-cited: (a) 02-fused-softmax's 'numerically stabilized' single-pass softmax is the online-softmax idea (Milakov & Gimelshein 2018, arXiv:1805.02867) — the source does NOT cite it, so at most a prereq-box may reference it as unverified-candidate context, do not attribute to the tutorial. (b) 09-persistent-matmul's Stream-K-style persistent scheduling / TMA relate to Osama et al. Stream-K (arXiv:2301.03598) and NVIDIA Hopper TMA docs — again uncited in source; treat as optional citation only. 07-extern-functions points to CUDA libdevice-users-guide and ROCm device-libs (vendor docs, not papers).

docs_pages_survey_citations.note: The Triton programming-guide (docs/programming-guide/) is adapted from Tillet's PhD work and carries a literature survey. These are background/positioning chapters, NOT tutorial topics. All refs below are written verbatim in the .rst with venue+year (source-cited); grounding_need for essentially all of them is 'citation' (one-line mention in a Related-Work / Introduction background chapter). Verify arXiv ids at write time only for any promoted to prereq-box.

foundational_paper_not_in_refs.where_used: NOT cited as a reference in tutorials/docs, but the programming-guide (chapter-1 introduction.rst, chapter-2 related-work.rst) is a direct adaptation of this paper / Tillet's dissertation.
